naya.summary: The safest route is stabilize the fixed result pipeline, extract a pure deterministic scoring engine, lock an assessment contract, then generalize to topic-driven generation. Do not rebuild the house.
lessons: Concrete gaps include E02 selector/version mismatch, competing external results navigation, hard-coded scoring, missing dynamic-generation schema/validator, and insufficient automated regression coverage.
Generation must be provider-abstracted, cached, rate-limited, schema-validated, and separated from zero-cost deterministic scoring.

human.summary: We already have a strong MAXESS foundation. The smartest path is to repair the result boundary first, make scoring its own reliable engine second, and only then make assessments work for any subject.
lessons: Fix the foundation before adding the ocean.
One result object and one scoring authority should feed every results section.
